title: Deterministic relative date humanizer
instructions:
Implement the four-method `Humanizer` class in `humanizer.py`. No method reads the clock.

## Files
- `humanizer.py`

- `Humanizer(now)` stores the supplied reference `datetime.datetime`. Non-datetimes
  raise `TypeError`.
- `seconds_from(moment) -> int` returns `(moment - now).total_seconds()` truncated
  toward zero. A non-datetime raises `TypeError`; mixing naive and timezone-aware
  datetimes raises `ValueError`. A datetime is aware when `utcoffset()` is not None.
  Aware values with different UTC offsets must compare as instants.
- `describe(moment) -> str` uses the signed integer from `seconds_from`. Zero is
  `just now`. Otherwise choose the largest unit whose size is at most the absolute
  seconds: week=604800, day=86400, hour=3600, minute=60, second=1. Divide with floor
  division; do not round and do not include smaller units. Pluralize unless the count
  is 1. Past is `N units ago`; future is `in N units`. Examples: `3 days ago`,
  `in 1 hour`. There is no month/year unit: large durations remain weeks.
- `describe_many(moments) -> list[str]` accepts any iterable and returns descriptions
  in input order, including duplicates; an empty iterable gives `[]`. Invalid
  moments raise the same errors as `seconds_from`.
